idiom_name: record - normalize - compare - approve loop over a committed reference artefact
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: (1) assemble a stimulus set of real inputs for the subject; (2) run the subject unchanged and capture everything observable - return values, stdout and stderr, produced files, protocol traffic, rendered output; (3) normalize or redact the volatile and sensitive parts (timestamps, identifiers, paths, addresses, collection order, locale) so a failure means a behavioural change; (4) commit the captured result as the reference artefact; (5) on every later run re-capture, apply the same normalization and compare, reporting the first meaningful difference; (6) make re-recording a separate, explicit mode that a human approves, and let CI only verify. Keep detection (the comparison) and approval (accepting a new reference) strictly separate. For AI/ML outputs, supplement byte-diff with statistical thresholds (edit distance, cosine similarity on embeddings, KS-test on distributions).
code_sketch:
for input in corpus:                     # production-derived + boundary inputs
    got = normalize(run(subject, input))  # capture, then mask volatile parts
    if mode == RECORD:                    # explicit, local, reviewed step
        write(golden_path(input), got)
    else:                                 # CI: verify only
        assert_golden(golden_path(input), got)   # show the diff, never write
pitfalls: Bulk re-recording: an update flag that rewrites every reference in one run converts the suite into a rubber stamp; re-record case by case and review the diff.
Encoding known defects: a reference artefact records the bug along with the behaviour, so the defect must be fixed (or explicitly marked) rather than approved silently.
Skipping normalization: timestamps, identifiers, temporary paths and collection order inside the reference produce flaky failures, after which the suite gets quarantined and dies.
Pinning the wrong surface: capturing internal structures or call sequences instead of observable output makes harmless refactoring fail - exactly what the net exists to permit.
Exact-match on LLM outputs: requiring byte-exact matches for stochastic model outputs creates massive CI flakiness; use statistical comparison instead.

Updating snapshots in a separate PR: the code change and the baseline change are decoupled, so reviewers cannot understand why the behaviour shifted; always pair the source change and the approval in one PR.

Cross-OS snapshot sharing: line endings, font rendering, and anti-aliasing differences between macOS/Linux/Windows make shared snapshots flaky; use environment-normalized comparisons or per-OS artefact suffixes.
Oversized monolith artefacts: one giant reference file for an entire page or session produces uninterpretable diffs; shard into per-component, per-scenario or per-phase artefacts.
Production data in artefacts: committing raw captured traffic with emails, tokens, or internal hostnames creates a secret-leak vector; always redact before committing.
sources: E. J. Weyuker. The Oracle Problem in Software Testing: A Survey. (IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering, vol. 29, no. 5, May 2003 / Computer.org CS续 2015) — Foundational survey on the oracle problem - characterizing when test oracles are unavailable or unreliable, directly motivating the characterization test pattern as a practical workaround.
https://www.computer.org/csdl/journal/ts/2015/05/06963470/13rRUx0geBw

Emily Bache. Why we should be saying 'Approval Testing' instead of 'Golden Master'. (ProAgile / Coding Is Like Cooking, 2020-2021) — Argument for dropping 'Golden Master' (implies immutability, problematic master/slave connotation) in favour of 'Approval Testing' which foregrounds human judgement in the review step.
https://proagile.se/blog/say-approval-testing-instead-of-golden-master

Marko Lauronen. Characterization Testing — refactoring legacy code with confidence. (Cloudamite, 2024) — Practical step-by-step guide: determinism preparation via injectable seams, coverage-guided corpus expansion, test generation from actual outputs, and incremental refactoring workflow.
https://cloudamite.com/characterization-testing/

Snapshot Testing in CI/CD Pipelines: Setup and Best Practices. (Helpmetest.com, 2025) — CI/CD-specific challenges: jest --ci behaviour, TZ/locale normalization, parallel runner snapshot integrity, automated snapshot update workflows via PR comments, CODEOWNERS governance.
https://helpmetest.com/blog/snapshot-testing-ci-cd-pipelines/

Pramod Dutta. Approval Testing and Golden Master Testing Guide. (QASkills.sh, 2026) — Comprehensive guide covering fixture selection, normalizer design, JSON/text/image approvals, generated code verification, diff quality, production data redaction, and governance.
https://qaskills.sh/blog/approval-testing-golden-master-guide

Snapshot Testing Governance Guide. (QASkills.sh, 2026) — Governance framework: snapshot tiering (Critical/Standard/Advisory), update vs fix decision tree, sanitization patterns for volatile fields, pruning rules, anti-pattern catalogue.
https://qaskills.sh/blog/snapshot-testing-governance-guide

jlevy/tbd. Golden Testing Guidelines. (GitHub jlevy/tbd) — Modern session-based golden testing: stable/unstable field classification, switchable mock modes (live vs mocked), CLI for AI agent testing, layered domain assertions alongside raw diff.
https://github.com/jlevy/tbd/blob/main/packages/tbd/docs/guidelines/golden-testing-guidelines.md

Core Concepts — franiglesias/golden (Go library). (DeepWiki, 2025) — Three-mode framework: Verification (standard snapshot), Approval (always-fail until explicit approval), Golden Master (combinatorial all-inputs capture) — maps cleanly to Feathers' characterization workflow.
https://deepwiki.com/franiglesias/golden/3-core-concepts

Ankush Choudhary Johal. Golden Master Approval: Snapshot Testing Hypothesis 2025. (johal.in, 2025) — Statistical extension of golden masters for AI/LLM outputs: edit distance + embedding cosine similarity + KS-test for non-deterministic model outputs; ML classifier approves within threshold, fallback to human review.
https://johal.in/golden-master-approval-snapshot-testing-hypothesis-2025

Automated LLM Evaluation: Building a CI/CD quality gate that actually runs. (Galtea.ai, 2026) — llm-eval-ci: golden dataset versioning, deterministic heuristic graders (grounding, hallucination, format), optional LLM judge backend, regression gate with per-grader thresholds, GitHub Actions integration.
https://www.galtea.ai/blog/automated-llm-evaluation-building-a-ci-cd-quality-gate-that-actually-runs

AI Evals in Production — AI Programming Manual. (AI Programming Manual, 2026) — Golden dataset design (60-120 cases), CI regression gates for prompts and model changes, hybrid scoring (rule-based + model-based), production observability, and a 30-day rollout playbook.
https://aiprogrammingmanual.com/aievals/

Kurt Zoglmann. Golden-Output Regression Test. (Abstractopedia / The Encyclopedia of Abstractions) — Academic framing of golden-output regression as a characterisation oracle: equivalence-preserving rewrite optimization, observable-behaviour boundary, comparison strictness tradeoffs, and pairing with metamorphic testing.
https://abstractopedia.org/mechanisms/golden_output_regression_test/

Exploring LLM-as-a-Judge for Validation and Verification Testsuites. (arXiv:2408.11729, 2024) — Pipeline-based LLM-as-judge for compiler test validation; agent-based approach (tool use + external info) increases accuracy; directly applicable as a semantic approver for characterization artefacts.
https://arxiv.org/html/2408.11729v1

A Self-Testing Framework for LLM Applications with Quality Gates. (arXiv:2603.15676, 2026) — Evidence-coverage-based release gate (PROMOTE/HOLD/ROLLBACK) for multi-agent LLM systems; five operationalized dimensions; Mann-Kendall trend analysis; evidence coverage as primary severe-regression discriminator.
https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.15676

Metamorphic Testing: Testing the Untestable. (arXiv / University of Seville) — Addresses the oracle problem by checking metamorphic relations (properties that must hold across multiple executions) rather than individual outputs; complements golden masters by providing correctness checks where exact reference is unavailable.
https://personal.us.es/sergiosegura/files/papers/segura20-software.pdf

Metamorphic Testing: A Review of Challenges and Opportunities. (University of Washington / CSE 503) — Survey of metamorphic testing state of the art; oracle problem context; MR identification strategies; integration with mutation analysis; applicability to AI/LLM testing.
https://homes.cs.washington.edu/~rjust/courses/CSE503/2021_02_12-reading2.pdf

An Empirical Evaluation of Property-Based Testing in Python. (ACM ICPC 2025 / ACM Digital Library) — Empirical study of 426 Python projects using Hypothesis: property-based tests kill ~50x more mutations than average unit tests; exception-checking, inclusion, and type-category properties most effective.
https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3764068

Prof. James A. Jones et al. Revealing Regressions: A Comparative Study of State-Capture Strategies in Validating Program Behavior. (FSE 2026, Spider Lab Research Group) — Empirical study of 12 real-world projects: systematic state-capture strategies outperform human-written assertions by avg 35.7% in regression detection; snapshot testing widely adopted but often under-utilized.
https://spideruci.org/publication/du-spectra-2026/

Mitchell Hashimoto. Testing with Golden Files. (mitchellh.com/writing) — Practitioner's guide to golden file testing: when to use, common pitfalls, comparison with other approaches; widely cited in Go and Terraform communities.
https://mitchellh.com/writing/golden-files

README — bkitduy/characterization-test-generator. (GitHub) — Claude Code plugin that auto-generates characterization tests for existing code; uses coverage-guided stimulus expansion, unstable field scrubbing, and mutation-based test effectiveness verification.
https://github.com/bkitduy/characterization-test-generator/blob/main/README.md
